language.script_notes: Latin alphabet with the diacritic letters č, ć, š, ž and đ. Road signs are blue with white lettering; the national flag's red-and-white checkerboard appears on municipal logos and crests. Serbian in Latin script looks similar, but Cyrillic is absent here.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White post with a red rectangle on the front and the same rectangle in white on the back.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Flat, slim post with a rectangular reflector.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Angular guardrails, sometimes painted in red-and-white stripes (a look shared with Serbia, Montenegro, Turkey and Poland).
road_furniture.line_paint: White edge and center lines; black-and-red chevrons mark curves.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Direction signs have a yellow background with a black outline, often with a pencil-shaped tip; pedestrian crossings show five stripes; narrow grey or blue fire hydrants are a common sight. Konzum supermarkets, Tisak kiosks and Plodine stores are common brands.

architecture.roof_style: Red terracotta tile roofs on the coast; steeper roofs on houses in the inland north.
architecture.roof_material: Clay tile is standard nationwide, with corrugated metal on utility buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Light stone and plaster houses with shutters near the sea; Habsburg-era masonry in the continental north; plastered family houses with tile roofs across the interior. See regional profiles for the coast/continental split.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Pale stone and white on the coast, yellow and ochre plaster inland.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Stone villages and walled towns on the Adriatic; Austro-Hungarian civic buildings in the north; socialist-era apartment blocks and holiday hotels; churches with bell towers.

nature.vegetation: Mediterranean scrub, olive groves and pines on the coast and islands; deciduous and beech forest in the mountains; corn, wheat and sunflower fields on the northeastern plains.
nature.terrain: A crescent-shaped country — a long, rocky karst coast with over a thousand islands, a mountainous Dinaric spine, and flat, fertile Pannonian plains in the northeast.
nature.climate_signature: Mediterranean along the coast, continental inland — bright, dry summers by the sea and colder winters in the north.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text; since 2016 with a blue EU strip on the left carrying 'HR', though older white plates without the strip are still seen in older Street View coverage.
vehicles.plate_format: Two-letter city code, then digits and letters (e.g. 'ZG 1234-AB'), with the code marking the town of registration.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: A standard Central European mix, with many tourist rental cars on the coast in summer.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3/4 with dense coverage; some older imagery still shows the pre-2016 plates.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense along the coast and main roads; good coverage of the interior.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar angular guardrails, related languages and Balkan architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The bollard's red rectangle is centered on the front with a white one on the back, whereas the Serbian one sits off to one side; Cyrillic Ђ and Ћ appear only across the border; the checkerboard shield is a strong tell.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Neighbouring Central European look, similar flat slim bollards
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Different bollard and signage details, and Slovenian plates and letters; the coast's karst and red tile roofs are more typical here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Adriatic stone architecture with terracotta roofs, especially in Istria
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Italian bollards have a red-diagonal front and street names use 'Via' and 'Piazza'; the coast's blue signage and centered red rectangle bollard point here.
